locked_abstract_paragraphs.text: 随机客流和路况变化使公交车头时距失衡，增加串车风险和乘客等待时间。驻站可调节车辆离站时刻，但受到车辆与站点差异、环境条件及动作上限的制约。强化学习可依据状态选择动作，却难以在实际运营中反复试错，最终策略又面临训练与使用环境的分布偏移，使其现实部署面临困难。本文围绕从仿真到现实的驻站控制，先研究未预先获得目标域训练数据时的平稳随机鲁棒学习与非平稳随机适应学习，再研究获得目标域离线数据后的跨保真训练及模型修正。

本文以车辆完成必要上下客后的到站事件为决策时刻，将车辆与站点信息、前后车头时距、驻站动作及乘客时间成本纳入统一控制模型。多线路实验沿用现有长沙公交路网、线路、乘客起讫点（Origin-Destination，OD）需求及时刻表资料。自建简易仿真用于低成本训练，城市交通微观仿真平台（Simulation of Urban MObility，SUMO）用于表示更细致的道路交通和车辆相互作用，作为现实环境的仿真代理。跨保真迁移采用SUMO离线数据与简易仿真中在线交互产生的新数据训练策略，再于未参与训练的SUMO运行场景中评价。本文公交控制研究统一采用单一驻站动作。主要研究内容与结果如下。

（1）针对不同车辆与站点的差异及随机运行中的动作价值估计波动，提出结合类别特征嵌入与连续状态的共享驻站策略，并提出鲁棒集成软演员评论家方法（Robust Ensemble Soft Actor-Critic，RE-SAC）。以候车时间的两倍与车内时间之和作为广义乘客时间，在学习器及训练设置一致的类别表征比较中，学习嵌入相对独热编码在正常运行、客流激增和快速切换下，分别降低5.51%、1.41%和4.91%的人均广义乘客时间。单一驻站动作、车头时距目标下，RE-SAC相对主流对照在所测随机环境中具有更低的计划时距偏差和更稳定的价值评价。结果表明，在高不确定性环境中，引入保守偏移以提高价值评价稳定性，可以带来更好的控制效果；但不同运营目标仍存在取舍。

（2）针对运行规律随时间变化、而驻站只能局部改变车辆离站时刻的问题，提出贝叶斯自适应策略正则化（Bayesian Adaptive Policy Regularization，BAPR），通过环境识别和模式置信调节形成条件适应；进一步提出因果符号贝叶斯自适应策略正则化（Causal-Symbolic Bayesian Adaptive Policy Regularization，CS-BAPR）。在正常需求、单次与重复环境变化、持续高需求及短时极端需求下，训练稳定化方法相对前序BAPR均降低平均时距奖励惩罚，单一驻站动作下的降幅为58.82%至69.79%。与RE-SAC的匹配比较表明，CS-BAPR在运行规律发生变化时具有更强的条件适应能力，其结构化输出并非在每种条件下都带来额外收益。改用乘客时间目标后，服务成本差异缩小，说明时距目标收益不能直接解释为同等幅度的乘客时间收益。

（3）针对现实目标环境难以持续通过试错采集训练数据的问题，在混合离线与在线强化学习（Hybrid Offline-and-Online Reinforcement Learning，H2O）及其改进框架（Improved Framework for Hybrid Offline-and-Online Reinforcement Learning with Dynamics Gaps，H2O+）基础上建立公交跨保真训练流程。固定SUMO离线数据与简易仿真交互共同支持策略训练，同时到站车辆编码、允许车辆不额外停站或增加驻站时长的单一驻站动作，以及运行末段载客较少且后续接续车辆不足时的完成保障，共同构成控制器。在十个新环境块、三档需求和九种控制器的1350次配对评价中，完成保障相对相同学习策略的直接父控制器，使窗口内人均广义乘客时间减少92.12秒、下降3.71%，完成率提高0.466个百分点。同更新预算比较支持混合训练方案相对纯离线方案的收益。

（4）针对源目标转移关系失配，提出基于模型修正的世界模型方法（Model-Corrected World Model，MC-WM），以留出预测误差选择残差修正或直接目标模型，并以对数置信评价加权一步模型样本。公交扩展采用固定目标离线数据与混合事件模型，并以归一化置信备份缓解模型作用衰减。单一驻站动作、乘客时间目标下，在正常标定、联合50%和联合75%源参数偏差三种条件下，相对采用共同完成保障的Daganzo式规则，人均广义乘客时间分别减少57.67、70.67和76.26秒。联合偏差同时改变道路平均速度、乘客OD、路口延误和基本停站服务时间等转移参数。车头时距目标下，高偏差条件下MC-WM相对H2O+也显示出改善。结果支持利用目标离线数据修正源仿真训练，并显示这一作用可服务于两种运营目标。
上述研究分别从随机性、运行变化、目标经验和预测修正四个方面，建立单一驻站策略应对训练与使用环境差异的方法。
在目标离线数据可获得时，本文以精细仿真历史数据提供目标运行经验，结合简易仿真交互训练，并在未参与训练的SUMO场景中检验策略泛化。这一信息分工为后续以真实公交历史记录替代SUMO离线数据、利用可交互仿真训练驻站策略提供了研究依据。
关键词： 公交驻站控制；鲁棒强化学习；分布偏移；仿真到现实；世界模型

Random passenger demand and changing road traffic disrupt bus headways, promote bunching, and increase passenger waiting time. Holding control regulates departure times, but its effectiveness depends on vehicle and stop characteristics, operating conditions, and the maximum permitted holding time. Reinforcement learning can select actions from operational observations, yet repeated trial-and-error learning on an operating fleet is impractical, and the resulting policy may encounter a distribution shift between training and deployment environments. This thesis studies sim-to-real bus holding control: robust learning under stationary stochastic conditions and adaptive learning under non-stationary stochastic conditions first address settings without pre-collected target-domain training data; cross-fidelity learning and model correction then incorporate target-domain offline data.

An arrival-event-based control model takes decisions after required passenger boarding and alighting and connects vehicle and stop information, forward and backward headways, a holding action, and passenger time costs. Multi-line experiments use an existing Changsha road network, bus routes, origin-destination (OD) demand, and timetables. An in-house simplified simulator supports low-cost training. Simulation of Urban MObility (SUMO) represents road traffic and vehicle interactions in greater detail and serves as a simulated proxy for the real operating environment. Cross-fidelity transfer combines SUMO offline data with new data collected through online interaction in the simplified simulator and evaluates the resulting policy in SUMO operating scenarios not used for training. All bus-control studies in the thesis use a single holding action. The main contributions and results are as follows.

To address differences among vehicles and stops and fluctuations in action-value estimates during stochastic operations, this thesis proposes a shared holding policy combining categorical feature embeddings with continuous observations and develops Robust Ensemble Soft Actor-Critic (RE-SAC). Generalized passenger time is defined as twice waiting time plus onboard time. With the same learner and training settings, learned embeddings reduce generalized passenger time relative to one-hot encoding by 5.51%, 1.41%, and 4.91% under routine operations, demand surges, and rapid switching. With a single holding action and a headway objective, RE-SAC achieves lower planned-headway deviation and more stable value evaluation than the tested mainstream baselines. These results show that introducing a conservative bias to stabilize value evaluation can improve control under high uncertainty, while different operating objectives retain tradeoffs.

To address changing operating laws and the limited ability of holding to alter departure times, this thesis proposes Bayesian Adaptive Policy Regularization (BAPR), using environment identification and operating-mode confidence adjustment, and subsequently develops Causal-Symbolic Bayesian Adaptive Policy Regularization (CS-BAPR). Across routine demand, single and repeated environmental changes, sustained high demand, and brief extreme demand, training stabilization reduces the mean headway-reward penalty relative to the preceding BAPR configuration by 58.82% to 69.79% with a single holding action. Matched comparisons with RE-SAC support stronger conditional adaptation when operating laws change, while structured policy outputs do not provide an additional benefit in every condition. Under a passenger-time objective, service-cost differences narrow, so headway gains cannot be interpreted as equal reductions in passenger time.

To reduce dependence on repeated trial-and-error data collection in the target operating environment, this thesis develops a bus-specific cross-fidelity workflow based on Hybrid Offline-and-Online Reinforcement Learning (H2O) and the Improved Framework for Hybrid Offline-and-Online Reinforcement Learning with Dynamics Gaps (H2O+). Fixed SUMO offline data and simplified-simulator interaction jointly support policy training. Simultaneous-arrival encoding, a single action that adds either no extra holding or a positive holding duration, and a completion reserve for late-operation states with low onboard loads and insufficient following service form the complete controller. In 1,350 paired evaluations covering 10 new environment blocks, three demand levels, and nine controllers, the reserve reduces within-window generalized passenger time by 92.12 seconds, or 3.71%, and increases completion by 0.466 percentage points relative to the direct parent with the same learned policy. An update-budget-matched comparison supports hybrid training over the tested offline-only scheme.

To address source-target transition mismatch, this thesis proposes the Model-Corrected World Model (MC-WM), selecting residual correction or direct target modeling using held-out prediction errors and weighting one-step model samples through log-confidence evaluation. The bus extension uses fixed target offline data and hybrid event models, with a normalized confidence backup limiting attenuation of model updates. With a single holding action and a passenger-time objective, generalized passenger time decreases relative to a Daganzo-style rule with the same completion reserve by 57.67, 70.67, and 76.26 seconds under calibrated, joint 50%, and joint 75% source-parameter mismatch, respectively. Joint mismatch changes road speeds, passenger OD demand, intersection delays, and required stopping-service times together. With a headway objective, MC-WM also improves over H2O+ under large source mismatch. These results support using target offline data to correct source-simulator training for both operating objectives.

The thesis connects stationary robust control, non-stationary adaptation, cross-fidelity transfer, and world-model correction through target-domain data availability. Its central mechanism combines records from a detailed simulator with interaction in a simplified simulator to learn holding policies that generalize to unseen SUMO scenarios. The results support replacing SUMO offline data with real bus-operation records and continuing training in an interactive simulator as a pathway from simulation toward real bus holding control.
Keywords: bus holding control; robust reinforcement learning; distribution shift; sim-to-real transfer; world models
